To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel stochastic channel models for MIMO wireless radio channels is proposed.

the proposed model is a) a novel MIMO channel model, that b) is valid for a wide range of MIMO scenarios, and c) is capable to better predict capacity, channel structure and channel correlation than state-of-the-art MIMO channel models.
we propose a novel stochastic MIMO channel modeling approach that is able to capture the joint correlation of both channel link ends.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new stochastic channel model, which allows a more realistic description of the spatial correlation properties in MIMO channels.
the development and validation of an improved stochastic model for the spatial structure of MIMO channels.
the derivation of a novel stochastic MIMO channel representation which can be used for the prediction of MIMO channel capacity and spatial channel characteristics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed model provides a better fit to the measured data, which is not only true for capacity and eigenmode correlation, but also for the spatial structure of the channel.
the proposed stochastic channel model is able to describe the joint correlation properties of the eigenmodes of transmitter and receiver in a very simple and elegant manner.
the proposed channel model is a very promising alternative to state-of-the art stochastic MIMO channel modeling, especially in the context of MIMO channel capacity estimation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a stochastic MIMO channel that is capable of modeling the joint correlation properties between both link ends.
we propose a stochastic MIMO model which describes the joint correlation of the link ends and we validate it by means of measured MIMO data.
we have proposed a novel MIMO channel model that is based on a joint correlation of both the transmitter and the receiver.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the joint spatial correlation properties of MIMO channels can be described by means of a novel stochastic MIMO channel representation, which allows for a more accurate prediction of channel capacity and spatial channel properties than state-of-the-art MIMO channel models.
the spatial structure of the MIMO radio channel can be described by a single correlation function that is independent of the antenna arrangement and can be easily estimated from measurements.
the spatial correlation structure is determined by the eigenbasis of the two link-ends, and not by the transmit weights and the eigenmodes at the receiver.
